Synopsis:
    Bolivia's $1.9B IMF deal faces mounting domestic resistance from civic groups, unions, and business leaders who are linking fuel subsidy cuts to IMF conditionality. The agreement still needs congressional and IMF Board approval, and could unlock $5B in additional multilateral financing. Key risks include political fragility (minister departure, lack of transparency on deal terms), currency pressure on the boliviano, delayed IMF disbursements, and growing questions about President Paz's ability to push through reforms. EM-focused investors are turning cautious after riding Bolivian bond gains.
